primary_source.name: Bhagavata Purana Sanskrit ITX (SanskritDocuments), candidate reference
primary_source.status: candidate_only; exact edition and terms not independently confirmed
primary_source.mirror_note: Per-chapter verse ranges came from the SanskritDocuments ITX metadata mirror. Selected candidate Sanskrit passages from Canto 1 chapters 1–19, Canto 2 chapters 1–10, Canto 3 chapters 1–33, Canto 4 chapters 8–24, and Canto 12 chapters 1–13 were consulted as narrative orientation during draft work; these were not full or verse-by-verse reviews. No new verse text was imported into the product by these draft expansions. The mirror has no declared license, and the exact edition remains unconfirmed. Selected candidate Sanskrit passages from Canto 5 chapters 1–26 were also consulted as narrative orientation; these were not full or verse-by-verse reviews. Chapter mappings and edition remain unverified. Canto 10 summaries also used a provisional Sanskrit verse dataset for narrative orientation; the dataset edition and chapter mapping were not independently verified, and no verse-by-verse review was performed.

source_policy.secondary_sources: Public-domain Dutt OCR may assist narrative orientation only; never treat OCR as verified source text.
source_policy.word_count_method: Whitespace-delimited tokens; used for triage only.

review_method.approach: Chapter-by-chapter comparison of each Nepali summary against the accepted reference text before only. Summaries are original Nepali prose; no source text and no copyrighted translation is copied into the app.
stages: draft_unverified - drafted, not checked against the accepted reference
source_checked - chapter mapping, verse range, sequence and narrative completeness checked against the pinned Wikisource revision, and the Nepali language pass completed
editorially_approved - a second, independent editorial sign-off
review_method.promotion_rule: A chapter is promoted individually, only when its own review record is complete. statuses are never bulk-promoted.
review_method.not_verified: source_checked means the summary agrees with the reference text at chapter level. It is not a verse-by-verse translation check, not a Sanskrit edition criticism, and not an endorsement of interpretive detail.

accepted_reference.name: श्रीमद्भागवतपुराणम् — Sanskrit Wikisource digital edition
accepted_reference.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (site-wide Wikisource licence); the underlying Sanskrit text of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa is public domain
accepted_reference.pin_method: Each reviewed chapter records the page id and revision id from the MediaWiki API (prop=revisions&rvprop=ids|timestamp), so the exact text read can be restored.
why_this_source: It is the only complete, openly licensed, externally hosted Sanskrit text reachable from this environment.
It carries per-chapter pages numbered exactly as the app's 335-chapter structure, so chapter mapping can be checked directly rather than inferred.
It is independently maintained and corrects known defects in the earlier candidate ITX dataset (see known_source_defects).
limitations: It is a volunteer transcription, not a critical edition; it does not record manuscript variants.
Individual pages occasionally omit or concatenate a verse number (for example 4.21 has no verse 45), so a missing marker is recorded as a source defect rather than treated as a content error.
Some pages add a पाठभेद note for a variant reading.
It is a Sanskrit text only. There is no authorized Nepali translation in use; Nepali wording is the app's own drafting, checked for language quality but not attributable to a translator.
accepted_reference.copyrighted_material: No copyrighted translation or purport (for example Bhaktivedanta Swami or Gita Press material) is used for verification or imported into the app.

rejected_or_limited_sources.SanskritDocuments ITX (bhagpur.itx): Rejected as the verification authority. Its own header states the file is not to be copied or reposted without permission, which makes it unsuitable as a redistribution basis, and it is a volunteer file with no edition statement.
rejected_or_limited_sources.Sahib45-here ITX-derived CSV dataset: Not used for verification. It is a re-parse of the same ITX, declares no licence, and so cannot independently corroborate it. It was used earlier only for draft orientation.
rejected_or_limited_sources.GRETIL sa_bhAgavatapurANa.txt: Rejected as authority after examination. It is a valuable academic corpus but this file has mis-numbered chapter boundaries: chapter 3.31 is truncated at verse 21 and the remainder is renumbered as 3.32 (which then runs 1-48 while 3.32 should have 43), and 4.21 is renumbered 1-52 instead of 1-53. Verse-count comparison against the accepted reference differs in 13 chapters.
rejected_or_limited_sources.Manmatha Nath Dutt public-domain English: Not usable here: archive.org is unreachable from this environment, the OCR is acknowledged as defective, and the translation gives no verse numbers. Retained only as a historical drafting aid.

known_source_defects.description: Verse-boundary defects observed in the accepted reference while reviewing. They are recorded so a later reviewer does not mistake them for summary errors.

entries.issue: Verse 45 is absent from the page; markers run 1-44 then 46-53, and the colophon of chapter 21 follows. The chapter therefore has 52 transcribed verses where the standard count is 53.
The page marks 39 verses and carries no marker for verse 10 (earlier candidates give 40). Verse text is continuous and the summary check is unaffected; the count is recorded as 39.

review_tooling: tools/ws-review.js - emits the raw-wikitext and revision-pin URLs for a chapter, measures a saved snapshot's verse range, and audits manifest consistency
tools/name-consistency.js - flags near-duplicate Devanagari spellings of the same proper noun across chapters
